questions.question: Which word means 'a way of looking at or thinking about something'?
questions.explanation: Your perspective is your own way of seeing or thinking about something — two friends can read the same story and have different perspectives.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
questions.options: She has finished her homework already. | She has finish her homework already. | She have finished her homework already. | She finishing her homework already.
questions.correctAnswer: She has finished her homework already.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is has or have plus the past participle — 'has finished'. Well remembered!

questions.question: Which sentence is correct for a finished time in the past?
questions.options: I visited my grandmother last weekend. | I have visited my grandmother last weekend. | I visit my grandmother last weekend. | I am visiting my grandmother last weekend.
questions.correctAnswer: I visited my grandmother last weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Last weekend' names a finished time, so we use the past simple: visited. The present perfect never goes with a finished time word.

questions.question: Complete the first conditional: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
questions.options: will cancel | cancel | cancelled | would cancelled
questions.explanation: In the first conditional, the if-clause uses the present tense and the result uses will: If it rains, we will cancel.

questions.question: Which sentence means the same as 'If you do not train, you will not improve'?
questions.options: Unless you train, you will not improve. | Unless you train, you will improve. | If you train, you will not improve. | You will improve because you do not train.
questions.correctAnswer: Unless you train, you will not improve.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' — so 'unless you train' is another way of saying 'if you do not train'.

questions.question: Which word names all the living things in a place and the way they depend on each other?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem is a community of living things — plants, animals and more — working together in one place.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The vet ___ helped the injured eagle lives near the reserve.
questions.explanation: We use 'who' in a relative clause about a person — the vet is a person, so 'the vet who helped'.

questions.question: The mountain path was described as 'treacherous'. What does that tell you about the path?
questions.options: It was dangerous and not as safe as it looked. | It was wide and easy to walk on. | It was brightly lit at night. | It was closed for repairs.
questions.correctAnswer: It was dangerous and not as safe as it looked.
questions.explanation: Something treacherous is dangerous, often because it seems safer than it really is — a good word to treat with care!

questions.question: Read the sentence: 'Desert foxes, which rest in cool burrows during the day, come out to hunt when the sun sets.' When do desert foxes hunt?
questions.options: After the sun sets | In the middle of the day | Early in the morning | All day long
questions.explanation: The sentence says the foxes rest during the day and come out to hunt when the sun sets — so they hunt after sunset.

questions.question: Choose the correct past simple form: The engineers ___ a bridge across the valley.
questions.explanation: 'Build' is an irregular verb — its past simple is 'built', with no -ed ending.

questions.question: Read: 'Early printing presses changed the world because books could be copied quickly, so ideas travelled faster than ever before.' Why were printing presses important?
questions.options: They let ideas spread quickly through printed books. | They made books more expensive to copy. | They stopped people from writing letters. | They slowed down the sharing of ideas.
questions.correctAnswer: They let ideas spread quickly through printed books.
questions.explanation: The passage says books could be copied quickly, so ideas travelled faster — printing helped ideas spread.

questions.question: Choose the correct quantifier: We do not have ___ money left in the class fund.
questions.explanation: Money is uncountable, so we use 'much' — 'many', 'a few' and 'several' go with countable nouns like coins.

questions.question: Which word means 'very important or necessary'?
questions.explanation: Something crucial really matters — saving a little money each week is crucial if you want to reach a goal.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct reflexive pronoun: The twins taught ___ to swim.
questions.explanation: The twins are more than one person, so we use 'themselves' — and remember, 'theirselves' is not a real English word.

questions.question: Amina said, 'I am saving for a bicycle.' Which sentence reports her words correctly?
questions.options: Amina said that she was saving for a bicycle. | Amina said that I am saving for a bicycle. | Amina said that she is save for a bicycle. | Amina told that she was saving for a bicycle.
questions.correctAnswer: Amina said that she was saving for a bicycle.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'I' becomes 'she' and 'am saving' moves back to 'was saving'. 'Told' would need a person after it — she told me.

questions.question: Which word means 'a job that needs special training or education'?
questions.explanation: A profession is a job you train or study for — doctors, teachers and engineers all have professions.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the past continuous and past simple together correctly?
questions.options: The wind was howling when the power went out. | The wind was howl when the power went out. | The wind howling when the power went out. | The wind was howling when the power was went out.
questions.correctAnswer: The wind was howling when the power went out.
questions.explanation: The longer background action takes the past continuous ('was howling') and the sudden event takes the past simple ('went out').

questions.question: Complete the sentence: We stayed in the shelter ___ the storm passed.
questions.explanation: 'Until' links the two ideas in time — we stayed inside up to the moment the storm passed.

questions.question: Choose the correct participle adjective: The documentary about volcanoes was really ___.
questions.explanation: The documentary causes the feeling, so it is fascinating; the people watching it are fascinated.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the past simple passive?
questions.options: The film was directed by a famous artist. | The director filmed a famous artist. | The film directed a famous artist. | The director was filming an artist.
questions.correctAnswer: The film was directed by a famous artist.
questions.explanation: The passive puts the film first and uses 'was' plus the past participle: the film was directed by someone.

questions.question: Which order of adjectives sounds right in English?
questions.options: a beautiful old Italian painting | an Italian old beautiful painting | an old beautiful Italian painting | a beautiful Italian old painting
questions.explanation: English usually orders adjectives opinion, then age, then origin — beautiful (opinion), old (age), Italian (origin).

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: Everyone in the gallery was quiet. | Everyone in the gallery were quiet. | Everyones in the gallery was quiet. | Everyone in the gallery be quiet.
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone in the gallery was quiet.
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like 'everyone' take a singular verb — everyone was, everybody is, nobody has.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: Of all the stories we read this year, this one was ___.
questions.options: the most interesting | more interesting | interestinger | most interestingest
questions.explanation: Long adjectives make their superlative with 'the most' — the most interesting, the most exciting.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: ___ has left a telescope in the science room.
questions.explanation: In a positive statement about a person we use 'someone' — 'anyone' belongs in questions and negatives.

questions.question: Which word describes doing something too quickly, without thinking carefully?
questions.explanation: A hasty choice is made in a rush — many folk tales warn that hasty decisions bring trouble!

questions.question: Which sentence gives an instruction correctly?
questions.options: Mix the flour and water, then knead the dough. | Mixing the flour and water, then kneads the dough. | You mixes the flour and water, then knead the dough. | To mixed the flour and water, then kneading the dough.
questions.correctAnswer: Mix the flour and water, then knead the dough.
questions.explanation: Instructions start with an imperative verb — Mix, Knead, Stir — with no subject in front.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: I wanted to finish the chapter, ___ the library was closing.
questions.explanation: 'But' joins two ideas that pull in different directions — wanting to read, and the library closing.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: We have lived in this town ___ 2020.
questions.explanation: 'Since' goes with a starting point like 2020; 'for' goes with a length of time like four years.

questions.question: Which of these is an opinion, not a fact?
questions.options: Chocolate ice cream is the best flavour. | Ice cream is usually kept frozen. | Many shops sell ice cream in summer. | Ice cream can be made from milk.
questions.correctAnswer: Chocolate ice cream is the best flavour.
questions.explanation: 'Best' shows what someone thinks or feels — that is an opinion. The other sentences can be checked and proved.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The castle ___ the story takes place stands on a high hill.
questions.explanation: We use 'where' in a relative clause about a place — the castle is a place, so 'the castle where the story takes place'.

questions.question: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'rain'?
questions.explanation: 'Rain' and 'play' share the long a sound — ai and ay are two ways to spell it.

questions.question: Which word best describes a person who is nice and helpful to others?
questions.explanation: A kind person is friendly and helpful — being kind is about how you treat people, not how you look.

questions.question: Which sentence about a daily routine is correct?
questions.options: She brushes her teeth every morning. | She brush her teeth every morning. | She brushing her teeth every morning. | She is brush her teeth every morning.
questions.correctAnswer: She brushes her teeth every morning.
questions.explanation: With he, she or it, the present simple verb takes -es or -s: she brushes, he washes.

questions.question: Which word names the soft white pieces of frozen water that fall from winter clouds?
questions.explanation: Snow is frozen water that falls in soft white flakes when the air is very cold.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: Yesterday the children ___ to the park after school.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' tells us the action is finished, so the verb takes the past simple -ed: walked.

questions.question: Read: 'On Saturday, Layla will visit the museum with her aunt. They plan to take the bus at nine o'clock.' How will Layla travel to the museum?
questions.options: By bus | By car | By train | On foot
questions.explanation: The text says they plan to take the bus at nine o'clock — so Layla will travel by bus.
